title: Trees and binary search trees
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: What must be true before binary search on an array?
options: The array need not be sorted.

questions.prompt: Insert X between A and B: what should new X.next point to?
questions.answer: B, before changing A.next to X.

B, before changing A.previous to X.
B, before changing A.next to X.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: child — Node directly below a parent.
subtree — A node and all its descendants.
binary search tree — A binary tree ordered by values, with smaller keys to the left and greater to the right.
balanced — Height kept relatively small compared with node count.

blocks.title: Start at root
blocks.text: Compare the new value 25 with root 40; it belongs in the left subtree.

blocks.title: Compare again
blocks.text: 25 is greater than 20, so move right. The right child currently stores 30.

blocks.title: Insert without breaking the property
blocks.text: 25 is smaller than 30; insert it as the left child of 30.

blocks.title: Worked example · Confirm and explain
blocks.text: 12 > 10, so 12 becomes the right child of 10.
